title: Fake News and Misinformation About Grant Changes
description: SASSA has dismissed false claims circulating on social media that double grant payments will be made in June. SASSA National Spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi called the reports 'untrue' and urged the public to reject them. SASSA also disputed claims that 'new rules could affect your pension' from 10 June 2025. Grant increases only happen when announced by the Ministry of Finance — the last increase took effect in April 2025 and the next is scheduled for October 2025. Any other increase claims are lies. The purpose of these rumours is to panic beneficiaries into sharing personal details or visiting fake websites.
indicators: Claims of urgent rule changes or suspensions
Promises of extra or double payments
Directs to fake websites or phone numbers
Spreads via WhatsApp groups and Facebook
No official SASSA branding or .gov.za links
Creates false urgency with specific dates
prevention: Verify all information on the official SASSA website (www.sassa.gov.za), official SASSA Facebook page (SASSANewsZA), or call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11. SASSA never announces grant increases or rule changes through unofficial social media channels. Only the Ministry of Finance and SASSA official pages are credible sources.
examples: SASSA will pay double grants in June 2025 — check your status now
New SASSA rules from 10 June 2025: Update your details or lose your pension
SASSA alert: Grants suspended unless you verify now at this link
Extra R500 grant payment for seniors — apply before the deadline
officialResponse: SASSA National Spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi said: 'These reports are untrue and should be rejected with the contempt they deserve. Any other increase not announced by credible and relevant authorities should be treated as lies.' Beneficiaries should only rely on credible sources on SASSA's official social media pages.

title: Postbank Card Fraud Impersonation Scams
description: Fraudsters posing as Postbank or SASSA officials visiting homes to 'assist' with card replacements or updates, stealing card details or demanding fees.
indicators: Home visits claiming to be officials
Requests for card PINs or details
Demands processing fees
Uses fear of grant suspension
prevention: SASSA and Postbank do not make unsolicited home visits for card issues. Replace cards only at official branches and never share PINs.
examples: We're from Postbank to update your SASSA card – give us your PIN
Pay R100 fee for new black card activation

title: Illegal Grant Card Loan Schemes
description: Scammers retaining SASSA cards and IDs to offer unauthorized loans against grants, charging high fees or stealing payments.
indicators: Offers loans using your grant card as collateral
Retains your card or ID
Promises quick cash with fees
Operates in communities without official approval
prevention: SASSA has zero tolerance for fraud; never hand over your card or ID. Report to police and SASSA immediately.
examples: Borrow R2000 now using your SASSA card – we'll deduct from your grant
Give us your card for a loan approval today

title: Unlawful Deductions by Unauthorized Insurers
description: Insurance companies deducting premiums from grants without beneficiary consent, often through misleading sales or forged agreements.
indicators: Unexpected deductions on pay day
Policies you don't recall signing
Calls from unknown insurers
Small recurring amounts deducted
prevention: Monitor your grant payments closely. Dispute via SMS to 34548 or at SASSA offices. Only authorize deductions in writing.
examples: R50 deducted for 'funeral policy' you never agreed to

title: Illegal Sale of SASSA Queue Positions
description: SASSA has condemned the unlawful selling of queue positions at its offices, where people charge beneficiaries for a place in line. SASSA CEO Themba Matlou called it a serious exploitation of vulnerable beneficiaries, especially the elderly and people with disabilities. SASSA is strengthening security and working with law enforcement to act against sellers and any officials who enable the practice. Source: South African Government media statement, 16 April 2026.
indicators: People selling a spot in the queue at SASSA offices
Payment demanded before you can enter or be seen
Targets elderly and disabled beneficiaries
Sellers claim they can guarantee you are seen faster
prevention: Never pay for a queue position. Arrive early, use online or eLife Certification self-service where possible, and report anyone selling queue positions to the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11. Source: https://www.gov.za/news/media-statements/sassa-condemns-illegal-sale-queue-positions-its-offices-16-apr-2026
examples: Pay R100 and I will hold your spot in the queue
Give me the money and I will make sure you get seen first
